rows.behaviorContract: Creating an ADR atomically commits one decision record plus initial applies-to, domain, and active-status connections, and the collapsed ADR is active and conflict-free.
rows.haskellTestName: create commits complete active ADR graph atomically

rows.behaviorContract: A single-head amendment inherits omitted decision fields while committing a complete immutable decision snapshot with a new head.
rows.haskellTestName: single-head amend inherits fields into full snapshot

rows.behaviorContract: An amendment whose effective state is unchanged is rejected and leaves the repository tip and committed object set untouched.
rows.haskellTestName: no-op amend is rejected without a commit

rows.behaviorContract: Parallel decision heads remain visible as a semantic conflict until an ordinary amendment explicitly reconciles them into one head.
rows.haskellTestName: parallel amendments remain visible until reconciled

rows.behaviorContract: Scope mutation supports expand, contract, mixed delta, and full replacement while producing the expected effective scope at each revision.
rows.haskellTestName: scope supports expand contract mixed and replace

rows.behaviorContract: Scope mutations reject invalid deltas and effective no-op changes without creating a commit.
rows.haskellTestName: invalid or empty scope changes are rejected

rows.behaviorContract: Divergent scope heads produce a conflict that can only be reconciled by an explicit complete scope set.
rows.haskellTestName: parallel scope heads require explicit full resolution

rows.behaviorContract: Obsolete ADRs are hidden from default reads, while reactivation restores visibility without discarding prior status history.
rows.haskellTestName: obsolete ADR hiding and reactivation preserve history

rows.behaviorContract: Obsoleting an ADR may name an active replacement and the collapsed status exposes that replacement relationship.
rows.haskellTestName: obsoletion records an active replacement

rows.behaviorContract: Decision and scope mutations are rejected while an ADR is obsolete, with no repository commit created.
rows.haskellTestName: obsolete ADR rejects amend and rescope

rows.behaviorContract: Parallel status heads remain auditable and are reconciled by appending a resolution rather than rewriting either head.
rows.haskellTestName: parallel status heads resolve append-only

rows.behaviorContract: Merging obsoletion against amendment exposes the status/decision coverage conflict and permits an append-only reactivation resolution.
rows.haskellTestName: obsolete-versus-amend merge exposes and resolves conflict

rows.behaviorContract: Deleting an ADR's initial domain revision makes doctor report both missing historical content and an incomplete operation.
rows.haskellTestName: missing initial domain revision is incomplete

rows.behaviorContract: Domain input normalization accepts single-segment root domain names and canonical dotted names while producing one stable canonical representation.
rows.haskellTestName: domain input canonicalizes root and dotted names

rows.behaviorContract: Invalid, duplicate, ancestor-redundant, or otherwise noncanonical domain sets are rejected without advancing Git history.
rows.haskellTestName: invalid or redundant domains do not commit

rows.behaviorContract: A domain refinement mapping must name a strict dotted descendant rather than the same domain or an unrelated domain.
rows.haskellTestName: domain refinement requires strict descendant

rows.behaviorContract: The root domain can be refined to a canonical dotted child and the ADR's effective classification follows the new revision.
rows.haskellTestName: root domain refines to dotted child

rows.behaviorContract: Domain refinement is committed as one append-only operation and history exposes both the prior and refined classifications.
rows.haskellTestName: domain refinement is one visible append-only operation

rows.behaviorContract: Domain mutation supports expansion, contraction, replacement, clearing, and later re-adding while preserving revision history.
rows.haskellTestName: domains expand contract replace clear and re-add

rows.behaviorContract: Decision amendment cannot alter domains through a backdoor and correctly inherits the latest refined domain set.
rows.haskellTestName: amend inherits refined domains without changing them

rows.behaviorContract: Domain changes require an active ADR and an effective nonempty delta; violations do not create commits.
rows.haskellTestName: domain changes require active ADR and nonempty delta

rows.behaviorContract: Domain query filters include descendants hierarchically and combine repeated filters by intersection rather than union.
rows.haskellTestName: domain filters are hierarchical and intersect

rows.behaviorContract: The public CLI refines domains and emits the stable compact JSON response and exit behavior promised by the public contract.
rows.haskellTestName: CLI domain refinement returns stable JSON

rows.behaviorContract: Queries at an old release and at main retain revision-local domain classifications after later changes on another line.
rows.haskellTestName: domain classification remains revision-local

rows.behaviorContract: Divergent domain refinements merge into an explicit domain conflict and an append-only operation reconciles them.
rows.haskellTestName: divergent domain refinements conflict then reconcile

rows.behaviorContract: Automatic stable/release/feature merging exposes the semantic decision conflict and one resolution propagates consistently across affected lines.
rows.haskellTestName: release merge semantic conflict resolves once and propagates

rows.behaviorContract: A release merge reports independent scope, domain, and status conflict axes and resolves each with stable post-resolution state.
rows.haskellTestName: release merge reports and resolves all conflict axes

rows.behaviorContract: The complete public ADR lifecycle performs exactly one commit per successful mutation and all public read models remain consistent.
rows.haskellTestName: complete public lifecycle commits once per mutation

rows.behaviorContract: Structured JSON input is accepted and prompt, input, and context digest provenance is retained in committed operation results.
rows.haskellTestName: structured JSON preserves digest provenance

rows.behaviorContract: Structured JSON rejects unknown or malformed fields and amendment input cannot use JSON to change domains outside the domain mutation API.
rows.haskellTestName: structured JSON is strict and blocks domain backdoor

rows.behaviorContract: Every failed public mutation preserves the repository tip and leaves no partial committed operation.
rows.haskellTestName: failed public mutations create no commits

rows.behaviorContract: The command parser exposes exactly the supported public commands and does not advertise unimplemented operations.
rows.haskellTestName: parser exposes exactly supported public commands

rows.behaviorContract: Reads are isolated to the committed tree, while doctor and mutations explicitly reject a dirty managed worktree file.
rows.haskellTestName: reads use committed tree while dirty mutations fail

rows.behaviorContract: Rewriting an immutable object remains an append-only violation even when its internal semantic digest and capsule are resealed.
rows.haskellTestName: resealed rewrite still violates append-only history

rows.behaviorContract: Deleting an immutable managed object is diagnosed as missing historical content and makes its operation incomplete.
rows.haskellTestName: deleted immutable object is missing and incomplete

rows.behaviorContract: Renaming a managed object is diagnosed both as a noncanonical destination and as deletion of its immutable canonical path.
rows.haskellTestName: renamed object diagnoses destination and deletion

rows.behaviorContract: Doctor reports malformed capsule data and an invalid semantic digest as integrity issues without crashing.
rows.haskellTestName: doctor survives invalid capsule and digest

rows.behaviorContract: The integrity scan rejects the same object identifier appearing at more than one managed path.
rows.haskellTestName: duplicate object identifier is detected

rows.behaviorContract: A valid historical revision remains queryable even when the current HEAD contains corrupt managed data.
rows.haskellTestName: historical revision remains queryable after HEAD corruption

rows.behaviorContract: Capsule field types are validated independently of a matching resealed semantic hash.
rows.haskellTestName: resealed semantic hash cannot hide capsule type errors

rows.behaviorContract: Human-readable decision frontmatter remains subject to schema validation after an attacker reseals the document.
rows.haskellTestName: resealed decision still validates frontmatter

rows.behaviorContract: Connection graph fields that require arrays reject scalar or object substitutions even when the document is resealed.
rows.haskellTestName: resealed connection rejects non-array graph fields

rows.behaviorContract: Every object in one operation must share identical prompt, input, and context provenance digests.
rows.haskellTestName: operation members share provenance digests

rows.behaviorContract: An operation that cites a basis commit unavailable from the repository is diagnosed explicitly rather than silently accepted.
rows.haskellTestName: unavailable basis commit is explicit

rows.behaviorContract: An amendment whose parent record is missing produces an integrity issue and is not silently collapsed into current ADR state.
rows.haskellTestName: amendment with missing parent is not collapsed

rows.behaviorContract: Scope reduction diagnoses self-cycles and deltas whose additions and removals do not form a valid transition.
rows.haskellTestName: scope self-cycle and invalid delta are diagnosed

rows.behaviorContract: The declared domain refinement mapping must exactly explain the committed domain delta.
rows.haskellTestName: domain refinement mapping matches committed delta

rows.behaviorContract: An obsolete status pointing to an unknown replacement ADR is diagnosed even when the status object is otherwise correctly sealed.
rows.haskellTestName: unknown status replacement is diagnosed

rows.behaviorContract: A status event whose declared transition disagrees with its stored state is detected as an integrity violation.
rows.haskellTestName: status event and state mismatch is detected

rows.behaviorContract: One operation group cannot contain objects belonging to different ADR identities.
rows.haskellTestName: cross-ADR operation group is rejected
